first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and the inherited evidence supports shortening onboarding and simplifying signup for self-serve accounts. I will verify both records before committing because they may involve overlapping changes and different downstream effects. A small guarded test is preferable to broad pricing intervention: measure completion and activation while preserving qualified-revenue, retention, and lead-quality guardrails so a superficial conversion lift is not mistaken for sustainable value.

final.rationale: Run a self-serve onboarding simplification experiment this week, prioritizing the shortened flow supported by memory_86 and incorporating signup simplification only for SMB accounts as supported by memory_31. This directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion and 6% activation declines while the verified evidence shows improved time-to-value, retention, activation, and qualified revenue. Guard against superficial gains by monitoring 30-day retention and qualified revenue; the observed SMB retention decline from signup simplification remains a downstream risk. Exclude non-SMB segments from the signup-field change and avoid broad promotional pricing, which could acquire lower-quality revenue despite competitor pressure.
